bluf: FindLaw, at lawyermarketing.com, is the Thomson Reuters law firm marketing business by its March 2024 capture, selling small US law firms websites, search, directory placement and call answering, and claiming 17,000+ of them. The record is thin and stale: the site is known only from that 2024 archive capture with no sitemap change since, with 0 clients on record and low confidence. Current evidence is its LinkedIn advertising: 22+ company ads in Sept 2026 selling a 2-minute AI visibility assessment to lawyers. A rival should know it sells paid search with no Google ads of its own, its publishing is idle, and the Monsoon read puts displacement at 74.8.
doing:
The positioning line, a one stop law firm marketing provider for small firms, decodes as: one vendor selling a small practice its website, search, directory listing and phone answering on one bill, anchored on the Thomson Reuters directory network. The headline claim, over 17,000 small law firms use its marketing services, with 3x more contacts and 48 awards in 2023, is a claim the record does not audit; even the owner line is dated to the March 2024 capture.

The sold mix runs 12 lines, from mobile friendly websites and PPC to call answering, Spanish language solutions and performance reporting. The capability read scores Local 3 as the lead line (the Thomson Reuters directory network: Premium Profile and Spotlight listings, attorney ratings and reviews) and five core lines at 2: AI Search / GEO (the Sept 2026 LinkedIn ads), Creator & Influencer (Social Media Pro, Video Social Pro), Paid Search (a PPC page plus a Spanish language PPC offer), SEO (an SEO page) and Web & Product (websites lead the homepage list; website packages and Spanish websites). Proprietary items listed: the directory network's FindLaw Premium Profile and Spotlight Listing, a law firm growth calculator, the Legal Leader, Digital Marketing Accelerator and Social Media Pro slugs, and the 2-minute AI Visibility assessment. The record lists no partners.

AI posture in plain terms: the only AI evidence is advertising, the Sept 2026 LinkedIn ads selling a 2-minute assessment and AI legal answer data, with no AI service page captured. The one dated move is the 2023 award claim, 48 national awards. Pricing signals: a range of web marketing packages and a solo practitioner offer, free consultation and Request a Quote, no prices captured. Conspicuously absent for a vendor of its size: no clients, case studies, news or jobs in the record, no offices, no founding date or headcount, and a sitemap of 671 URLs with nothing updated in 90 or 365 days.
clients:
FindLaw serves small law firms, the record's icp, in a single vertical, Legal, with the US as the home market and no offices listed.

The record holds 0 clients: no case study, testimonial, press release or logo wall was captured, so there is no named client, no observed need, no need mix and no shared client to report. The only sizing of the book is the homepage claim that 17,000+ small law firms choose its marketing services, a claim rather than a roster. What those firms come for is inferred entirely from what it leads with: local and lead generation through the Thomson Reuters directory network (Premium Profile and Spotlight listings, attorney ratings and reviews), web build through website packages and Spanish websites, organic demand through SEO and blogs, paid performance through PPC, social through Social Media Pro, and call answering and web chat for the phone. The record is silent on whether any of that work produced a described result.

Shared clients: none can be named, because none are named. A rival cannot read this book from the record; it can only read the offer.

What the base needs next: the Horus read ties it to KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation) and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers) as tailwinds and KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) and KJ7 (local discovery is being enclosed) as headwinds. It is likely, low confidence given no client evidence, that small firms buying directory placement next ask whether AI answers cite them, the exact question its Sept 2026 LinkedIn ads sell (the ad copy opens with a claim that 86% of AI generated legal answers refer, truncated in the capture); the directory model itself sits under KJ7.
house: Say and do: 1 of 2 tested lines is practised on its own house. Creator & Influencer is corroborated: its own short form channels are linked from the site (youtube). Paid Search is contradicted: it sells paid search and runs no Google ads of its own in the Transparency Center (status none, 0 ads). AI Search / GEO is unknown: the llms.txt check did not complete. The cadence test was not measured, but the sitemap read is flat: 671 URLs, 0 updated in 90 days, 0 in 365 days, 0 AI URLs. Tag stack onetrust only; CMS WordPress; no pixels, test tools or ABM stack. LinkedIn: active, 22 company page ads and 0 thought leader ads; 36 ads match the name query and more pages exist, so 22 is a floor. Sample: 'AI is already recommending attorneys to your potential clients. The data is in.' Meta and TikTok: no record.
market:
The Horus read gives a tailwind index of 14.8, band Favored, verdict Favored (+15). Best placed for KJ1 (the click is being replaced by the citation, net 0.257), driven by AI Search / GEO (+2) and Paid Search (+1) against SEO (-1), and KJ2 (ads inside AI answers, net 0.206). Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out, net -0.159), driven by Paid Search, SEO and Content & Digital PR, and KJ7 (local discovery is being enclosed, net -0.119), driven by Local (-1), its lead line. Best scenario fit: The Walled Oasis (41/100). Moves: making P1, partial on P3 (no LSA or Sponsored Places work), P4 and P7, absent on P2, P6 and P8, unknown on P5.

The Monsoon read gives index 68.8, band Onshore wind, inferred. Displacement 74.8 runs well above migration 62.8: an SMB book that buys on price, while Local (15) and SEO (11) carry the most movable hours. No hub office is listed, so the footprint is inferred, with a shore split of 65% South and Southeast Asia and 25% Latin America.
openings: It is very likely (high confidence) that price is the lead: displacement 74.8 on the Monsoon read and an SMB icp mean an offshore delivered rival can undercut the packages line by line, and the record lists no public pricing model (P5 unknown), so a transparent, outcome priced offer is a conversation it cannot have in public. The falsifier is a published price list or outcome pricing appearing on lawyermarketing.com. It is very likely (high confidence) that the paid search contradiction lands: it sells PPC to lawyers and runs no Google ads of its own, and P8 is absent, so the first legal agency to show results from ads inside AI assistants sets the price against it. It is likely (moderate confidence) that its directory anchored book is contestable under KJ7: local discovery is being enclosed and the read marks P3 partial, with no LSA or Sponsored Places work, so a rival that runs LSAs for small firms attacks the lead line. The idle sitemap (0 updates in 365 days) and the 2024 vintage of the record mean any current client is being served from an offer the record cannot see refreshed.
watch: I2, Alphabet Q3 2026 search growth and AI Mode ad disclosures (late October 2026): growth below 10% flags cannibalization of the SEO and PPC lines, and above 15% with AI Mode ads live confirms S1 and the KJ1 tailwind its AI visibility ads ride.
I10, Reddit US daily users against search referral volatility (late October 2026): US DAUq growth at or below 5% alongside AI Mode growth confirms the UGC starvation risk under KJ1.
I3, OpenAI ad run rate disclosures and CPM trend (rolling): the next $2B milestone and pricing below $20 CPM set the economics of ads inside assistants, where P8 is absent for FindLaw.

I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline (2 December 2026): new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas or engagement would touch the social lines it sells under KJ8.
Follow up whether the site changes from its March 2024 capture, since a refreshed sitemap or an AI service page would lift the low confidence on the whole record.
